## Purpose

This report compares the dataset produced by `Codex_Script.R`
(`Codex_Script_MergedData.csv`) with the original dataset
(`Merged_Data.csv`). Both files are read directly from `data/processed`, so
the tables update automatically if either file is regenerated.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(purrr)
library(knitr)

processed_dir <- if (dir.exists("data/processed")) "data/processed" else "../data/processed"
codex <- read_csv(file.path(processed_dir, "Codex_Script_MergedData.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
original <- read_csv(file.path(processed_dir, "Merged_Data.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

dataset_summary <- function(data, dataset) {
  tibble(
    dataset = dataset, rows = nrow(data), columns = ncol(data),
    countries = n_distinct(data$iso),
    first_year = min(data$year, na.rm = TRUE), last_year = max(data$year, na.rm = TRUE),
    unique_country_years = nrow(distinct(data, iso, year)),
    duplicated_country_year_rows = sum(duplicated(data[c("iso", "year")]))
  )
}
```

## Dataset structure

```{r}
bind_rows(
  dataset_summary(codex, "Codex script"),
  dataset_summary(original, "Original script")
) |>
  kable(caption = "Structural comparison of the two output files")
```

The Codex output is one row per country-year. The original output has
additional rows and duplicated country-year keys. These duplicates arise when more than one disaster record survives the merge: the original file retains`disaster_type`, whereas the Codex script collapses disaster records to the
binary `earthquake` and `drought` indicators before merging.

```{r}
all_columns <- union(names(codex), names(original))
tibble(
  variable = all_columns,
  in_codex_output = all_columns %in% names(codex),
  in_original_output = all_columns %in% names(original)
) |>
  kable(caption = "Variables included in each output file")
```

The Codex output uses consistent lower-case mortality names and adds
`armed_conflict`. The original output instead includes `disaster_type`,
`total_conflicts`, and `binary_conflict`; its mortality variable names retain
capital letters. Both outputs include all eight covariates: `gdp_1000`,
`oecd`, `pop_dens`, `urban`, `age_dep`, `male_edu`, `temp`, and
`rainfall_1000`.

## Country-year coverage

```{r}
codex_keys <- codex |> distinct(iso, year)
original_keys <- original |> distinct(iso, year)

tibble(
  comparison = c("Country-years in both files", "Only in Codex output", "Only in original output"),
  n_country_years = c(
    nrow(inner_join(codex_keys, original_keys, by = c("iso", "year"))),
    nrow(anti_join(codex_keys, original_keys, by = c("iso", "year"))),
    nrow(anti_join(original_keys, codex_keys, by = c("iso", "year")))
  )
) |>
  kable(caption = "Overlap in country-year keys")
```

The Codex script keeps the mortality data's 2000--2019 country-year frame.
The original file also contains 1999 records because its full join preserves
conflict data outside the mortality period.

## Agreement in comparable variables

For a fair value comparison, the original file is reduced to one row per
country-year. Repeated mortality and covariate values are represented by their
first non-missing value, while each disaster indicator is set to one if any
row for that country-year contains a one. This does not alter the source file;
it is only used for this comparison.

```{r}
first_non_missing <- function(x) {
  non_missing <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(non_missing) == 0) NA else non_missing[[1]]
}

original_key_level <- original |>
  rename(
    neonatal_mortality = Neonatal_Mortality,
    infant_mortality = Infant_Mortality,
    under5_mortality = Under5_Mortality
  ) |>
  group_by(iso, year) |>
  summarise(
    across(
      c(maternal_mortality, neonatal_mortality, infant_mortality,
        under5_mortality, gdp_1000, oecd, pop_dens, urban, age_dep,
        male_edu, temp, rainfall_1000),
      first_non_missing
    ),
    earthquake = as.integer(any(earthquake == 1, na.rm = TRUE)),
    drought = as.integer(any(drought == 1, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

comparable_variables <- c(
  "maternal_mortality", "neonatal_mortality", "infant_mortality",
  "under5_mortality", "earthquake", "drought", "gdp_1000", "oecd",
  "pop_dens", "urban", "age_dep", "male_edu", "temp", "rainfall_1000"
)

comparison_data <- codex |>
  select(iso, year, all_of(comparable_variables)) |>
  inner_join(
    original_key_level |> select(iso, year, all_of(comparable_variables)),
    by = c("iso", "year"), suffix = c("_codex", "_original")
  )

agreement <- map_dfr(comparable_variables, function(variable) {
  codex_value <- comparison_data[[paste0(variable, "_codex")]]
  original_value <- comparison_data[[paste0(variable, "_original")]]
  tibble(
    variable = variable,
    matched_non_missing = sum(!is.na(codex_value) & !is.na(original_value)),
    equal_values = sum(!is.na(codex_value) & !is.na(original_value) & abs(codex_value - original_value) < 1e-10),
    differing_values = sum(!is.na(codex_value) & !is.na(original_value) & abs(codex_value - original_value) >= 1e-10),
    missing_only_in_codex = sum(is.na(codex_value) & !is.na(original_value)),
    missing_only_in_original = sum(!is.na(codex_value) & is.na(original_value))
  )
})
```

```{r}
agreement |>
  kable(caption = "Value agreement after harmonising the original file to country-year level")
```

The mortality measures and covariates should agree wherever both files have a
value because they originate from the same raw CSV files. Any remaining
differences in `earthquake` or `drought` identify a difference in how the
multiple disaster records were combined.

## Conflict variables

The conflict indicators are not compared as identical columns because they
encode different definitions. `armed_conflict` in the Codex output first sums
battle-related deaths within each conflict-country-year, classifies a conflict
when the total is at least 25 deaths, and then lags that exposure by one year.
The original output retains `total_conflicts` and `binary_conflict` alongside
the merged records. Consequently, differences in these conflict fields are
expected and reflect the construction rule, not a merge error.

## Conclusion

The Codex output is the cleaner analysis-ready version: it has a unique
country-year key, explicit zeroes for absent disaster and conflict events, and
includes the requested covariates. The original output preserves extra
intermediate variables and event-level duplication, which is useful for
checking the original transformations but requires further aggregation before
country-year analysis.
